lesson.title: Fitting round a point
lesson.body: Shapes tile a floor when their corners fit round each point with no gap and no overlap. The angles round a point always add up to 360°.

lesson.title: The angle of a regular shape
lesson.body: A shape with n sides has angles that add up to (n − 2) × 180°. In a regular shape they are all equal: a regular hexagon has 4 × 180° = 720° in all, so each angle is 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

lesson.title: Three regular shapes tile
lesson.body: Only three regular shapes tile on their own: equilateral triangles (6 × 60°), squares (4 × 90°) and regular hexagons (3 × 120°). Each angle divides 360° exactly.

lesson.title: The others leave a gap
lesson.body: A regular pentagon has angles of 108°. Three make 324°, which leaves a gap of 36°, and four would overlap. So pentagons cannot tile on their own.

lesson.title: Any triangle, any four-sided shape
lesson.body: Copies of any triangle tile: two of each angle meet at a point, and 2 × 180° = 360°. Copies of any four-sided shape tile too: its four angles add up to 360°.

lesson.title: Two kinds of shape
lesson.body: Shapes of different kinds can fill a point together. Two regular octagons take 270°, and a square fills the 90° that is left, as on many tiled floors.

lesson.title: Three moves
lesson.body: A translation slides a shape: it still faces the same way. A reflection flips it over a mirror line: the image is its mirror image. A rotation turns it about a point: it is not flipped, but it points another way. In each, the shape keeps its size and its shape.

lesson.title: Mirror lines
lesson.body: In a reflection, the image is as far behind the mirror line as the shape is in front of it, and straight across from it.
